title: Asch Conformity Study: Exam-Style Stretch
welcome_lead: Evaluate Asch's study like a top-band candidate.
meta_desc: GCSE Psychology exam stretch on Asch: AO3 evaluation, ethics, validity and Perrin & Spencer.
final_note: You can write a balanced evaluation of Asch with named studies.

concepts.def: Confidence the IV caused the DV.
How well results apply outside the lab.
Whether findings hold across time periods.

walkthroughs.body_html: Asch's tight lab control gives high internal validity. Confederates and procedure were standardised, so results are replicable. The study sparked decades of follow-up work on conformity and group behaviour.

1. Temporal validity: Perrin & Spencer (1980) found near-zero conformity in UK students. 2. Androcentrism: only male US students. 3. Artificial task: judging lines lacks real-world consequence — low ecological validity.

'A student agrees with a wrong answer in class to fit in.' Use NSI to explain. Suggest Asch's dissenter variation: encouraging one friend to speak up could free others. Evaluate using Perrin & Spencer to question how strong NSI still is today.
